title: When the Orchard Falls
premise: In 1747, in the river town of Aldermoor, Jude Ravensworth inherits the unfinished atlas of her dead master, Elias Crane — an atlas that secretly charts a smugglers' route the Crown's surveyors were bribed to erase. When the autumn bridge closes and the King's men seal the valley, Jude discovers the atlas's final pages hold proof of a magistrate's treason, evidence that could hang half the town or free it. With the help of a ferryman's son who once betrayed her family, she must move the evidence past three checkpoints before the morning tide carries the ship — and her only chance at truth — out to sea. She succeeds at terrible cost: the atlas is published under Elias's name, her own part erased, and Jude must choose between the belonging she has finally found and the truth she cannot unlearn.
about_author: Marguerite Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing eighteenth-century survey maps in provincial English record offices. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Last Leaf of the Atlas
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Weeks after Master Crane's death, Jude works alone in the map shop, inking coastlines she doesn't understand. She finds a hidden pocket in the atlas's spine containing a chart that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: quiet grief curdling into unease as she realizes her master died with secrets.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She studies the hidden chart — a smugglers' cut marked in Crane's own hand — and notices the magistrate Wren's seal stamped on a copied page. The town prepares for the bridge's seasonal closing. Beat: denial; she wants history to stay elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The last cart crosses; the King's men post notices sealing the valley for winter. Jude watches the town's rhythms shift and realizes she is trapped inside whatever Crane was entangled in. Beat: claustrophobia, the world shrinking to Aldermoor.

chapters.title: A Visitor in Grey
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A Crown surveyor, Mr. Halloway, arrives ahead of the freeze, asking politely about Crane's papers. He leaves a card and a threat. Jude hides the chart inside a child's sampler. Beat: first fear, the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Son
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tam Corvane, who testified against Jude's brother years ago and broke her family, returns to town for winter work. Their first meeting is barbed and electric. Beat: resentment; old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude deciphers Crane's marginalia: the atlas's true final page proves Magistrate Wren sold the smugglers' route to the Crown and hanged the cutters to hide it. Beat: the burden of knowledge; loyalty to Crane's memory vs. terror of acting.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam maps the town's three barriers — the toll house, the church checkpoint, the quay gate — for his own reasons. He and Jude strike an uneasy bargain: he knows the guards; she knows the papers. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Sampler and the Sermon
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the church checkpoint, Jude passes the first barrier by hiding the chart in plain sight during a funeral sermon, with the vicar's widow — who loved Crane — as her unwitting shield. Beat: first small victory, and guilt over using kindness.

chapters.title: What Tam Did in Spring
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam confesses why he informed on Jude's brother: Wren coerced him, and the brother's exile was Wren's doing all along. Jude refuses to forgive. Beat: the theme sharpens — truth without mercy.

chapters.title: Halloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Halloway corners Jude: give up the chart and be protected; keep it and be tried as a smuggler's accomplice. He reveals Crane died running from Wren's men, not of age. Beat: rage and temptation to surrender.

chapters.title: The Orchard
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. In the abandoned orchard where Crane hid his proofs, Jude and Tam find the surveyor's original ledger — and signs someone else has been there. Beat: intimacy growing between them amid dread; belonging taking root.

chapters.title: A Traitor in the Shop
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The shop is ransacked; the decoy chart is gone. Jude realizes the widow's grandson has been reporting to Halloway. Beat: betrayal close to home; paranoia spreads through the town.

chapters.title: The Toll House Fire
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. To break the second checkpoint, Tam sets a diversionary fire at the toll house — but a guard is hurt, and Tam carries the guilt. Jude and the ledger slip through in the smoke. Beat: victory stained; the cost of loyalty to a cause.

chapters.title: Wren at the Door
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Magistrate Wren visits Jude, all courtesy, offering her Crane's old post and her brother's pardon if the ledger burns. She nearly says yes. Beat: the deepest temptation — belonging offered in exchange for silence.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Jude tells Tam she refused Wren. They plan the final run to the quay for the morning tide, knowing Halloway now expects it. Beat: resolve; two broken people choosing each other's cause.

chapters.title: The Widow's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The vicar's widow reveals she was Crane's correspondent — and that the ledger names her late husband too. She chooses truth at the cost of her name. Beat: memory as inheritance; courage passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The quay gate. Tam offers himself up as the smuggler Wren always said he was, buying Jude the minutes to cross with the ledger sewn into her coat. Beat: sacrifice; loyalty finally proven, not spoken.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the quay, Halloway intercepts her — but the ship's captain, an old ally of the hanged cutters, takes the ledger by force of numbers and sentiment. The ship sails with the proof aboard. Beat: climax; triumph that feels like loss.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wren, exposed by the ledger's copies, is arrested by his own superiors. Tam is released but marked. The town that whispered now applauds. Beat: justice arriving hollow, late, and public.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The atlas goes to press under Elias Crane's name alone. The publisher asks who finished it; Jude says no one. Beat: erasure chosen freely — she understands now why Crane hid his work.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The bridge reopens. Jude's brother returns with the tide; Tam waits at the crossing to face him. Forgiveness is not granted, only begun. Beat: belonging rebuilt slowly, without guarantees.

chapters.title: When the Orchard Blossoms
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A year later, Jude draws her own first map — of Aldermoor, complete, honest, signed. In the orchard, the trees bloom over Crane's grave. Beat: resolution; truth and belonging reconciled at last, memory kept by her own hand.
